Don't send him into school with a broken heart. 💔🏫

Busy morning. Theo is seven and he won't eat his breakfast. Mom's had enough: "Why are you ALWAYS like this?" By 9:00 he's sitting in spelling, and that sentence is sitting right there with him.

Here's what to do instead:
1️⃣ Notice the hurting quietly.
2️⃣ Comfort before correction.
3️⃣ Remember your words follow him all day.
4️⃣ Correct, don't break. "I love you."
5️⃣ Make a moment of connection. A hand squeeze. 🤝
6️⃣ Give him the words he needs. "You are loved."
7️⃣ Repair. "I'm sorry I yelled yesterday." 🩹
8️⃣ Say a loving goodbye. "You can always come to me."

Tuesday, Theo walks in with his whole heart. ❤️

"It is the LORD who goes before you. He will be with you; he will not leave you or forsake you. Do not fear or be dismayed." Deuteronomy 31:8 (ESV) 🙏 The same Jesus who walked out of the grave alive walks into that classroom with him.

So tuck a little note in his lunchbox: loved, safe, never alone. ❤️ And if your child drags their feet at the school gate, it might not be stubbornness. It might be worry.
